hlni.insight: The difference between B.Com and BBA is the analytical lens: B.Com focuses on quantitative financial accuracy, while BBA focuses on strategic management execution.
hlni.audienceGap: Students often assume one degree is inherently superior rather than understanding the different academic approaches.
hlni.viewerChange: Viewer shifts from comparing career outcomes to evaluating their own preference for financial analysis versus strategic planning.
hlni.support: Uses a 'Lens-Perspective' method to categorize academic engagement through a common business scenario (product launch).
hlni.payoff: The student identifies their own preference by testing which set of questions feels more natural to them.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: Finding Your Lens
objective: Help students identify their preferred analytical lens to make an informed degree choice.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: The Dilemma
shots.visual: A student sits at a desk looking between two brochures, looking overwhelmed.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA isn't about which is better. It’s about how you think.

shots.name: The Lens Method
shots.visual: The student writes on a whiteboard, splitting a 'Product Launch' case into two columns.
shots.dialogue: Look at a product launch. A B.Com lens asks: 'What is the cost?' A BBA lens asks: 'What is the strategy?'
shots.cameraPerformance: Static, clear view of the board.

shots.name: The Payoff
shots.visual: The student smiles, circles the 'Strategic' column, and puts the marker down confidently.
shots.dialogue: Which questions feel more natural to you? That’s your compass. Trust your own analytical style.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the comparison from degree prestige to internal analytical preference using a case-study lens.

selected.title: The 'Day-in-the-Life' Prompt
selected.audienceGap: Confusion about what 'Business' actually looks like in a lecture hall.
selected.hlni: The difference isn't the subject, it's the 'lens' applied (e.g., a B.Com student looks at the *cost* of a campaign, a BBA student looks at the *execution* of the campaign).
selected.viewerChange: Shifts perspective from 'Which degree is better?' to 'Which lens do I prefer?'
selected.concept: A relatable scenario of a marketing campaign used to show two different academic approaches.
selected.device: A single business case study presented from two distinct analytical viewpoints.
selected.support: Uses a common business scenario to illustrate academic differences; limited by the complexity of the scenario.
methodSteps: Pick one business case (e.g., a new product launch)
Write down one question about the 'money' (B.Com lens)
Write down one question about the 'people' (BBA lens)
selected.interpretationRule: Whichever set of questions feels more natural to you is your preferred analytical lens.
selected.visibleProof: The user writes on a whiteboard, splitting the case study into 'Financial Lens' vs 'Strategic Lens'.
selected.payoff: The student feels empowered to trust their own analytical style.
selected.limitations: This is a simplified pedagogical tool, not a professional assessment of degree content.

comparedWith.hlni: Degrees are distinguished by the 'Assessment Outcome'—what the student is specifically asked to demonstrate (e.g., technical accuracy vs. process-based application).
comparedWith.device: Split-screen comparison of two anonymous task descriptions, highlighting the specific verbs used (e.g., 'Calculate/Report' vs 'Propose/Defend').

comparedWith.hlni: The difference isn't the subject, it's the 'lens' applied (e.g., a B.Com student looks at the *cost* of a campaign, a BBA student looks at the *execution* of the campaign).
comparedWith.device: A single business case study presented from two distinct analytical viewpoints.

comparedWith.hlni: The 'core' subjects are often identical; the flexibility of electives is where the degree's true character is found.
comparedWith.device: Interactive visual where the viewer drags 'Interest Blocks' (e.g., Data, Strategy, Finance) into a degree grid.

conceptSelection.contrast: Trust uses a formal audit method to provide objective clarity. Connection uses a subjective 'lens' method to help the viewer identify their internal preferences. Discovery uses an interactive 'puzzle' method to highlight the overlooked role of electives in curriculum design.
